name: SCANA

summary.text: SCANA Corporation was the Cayce, South Carolina parent of South Carolina Electric & Gas. Its expansion of the V.C. Summer nuclear station with Santee Cooper was abandoned in 2017 after billions had been spent, much of it recovered from customers under state law. Former CEO Kevin Marsh and former executive vice president Stephen Byrne pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud for misleading regulators about the project's schedule; the SEC's civil case against SCANA and SCE&G was settled with a $25 million penalty and $112.5 million in disgorgement. SCANA was acquired by Dominion Energy in 2019.

facts.claim: Former SCANA CEO Kevin Marsh pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, admitting he intentionally defrauded ratepayers so that SCANA could obtain and retain rate increases and qualify for up to $2.2 billion in tax credits.
facts.quote: Marsh admits that he intentionally defrauded ratepayers, while he oversaw and managed the company's operations – including the construction of two reactors at the V.C. Summer Nuclear Station – so that SCANA could obtain and retain rate increases imposed on SCANA's customers and qualify for up to $2.2 billion in tax credits.

facts.claim: Former SCANA executive vice president Stephen Byrne pleaded guilty in July 2020 to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud under a cooperation agreement and was later sentenced to 15 months and ordered to pay over $1 million.
facts.quote: Stephen A. Byrne, former Executive Vice President of SCANA, pled guilty in federal court in July 2020 to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud under a plea agreement requiring him to cooperate with law enforcement officials.

facts.claim: The U.S. Attorney's civil division worked with the SEC to settle a lawsuit charging SCANA and SCE&G with defrauding investors through false and misleading statements about the nuclear expansion; the proposed settlement required a $25 million penalty and $112.5 million in disgorgement plus interest.
facts.quote: The proposed settlement would require SCANA to pay a $25 million penalty and require SCANA and SCE&G to pay $112.5 million in disgorgement plus prejudgment interest.

openQuestions: Site claim (convicted; ~$9 billion spent, much charged to customers; Marsh guilty plea and two years): the plea and sentence are supported; the $9 billion figure and the Dominion acquisition were not confirmed from the sources used.
The SEC settlement's final approval was not confirmed; the DOJ release describes it as proposed.
